Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

decontX 1.11.38

  • A new “Getting started” vignette, vignette("decontX", package = "decontX"), gives a short overview of DecontX and DecontPro, when to use each, and a quick example on simulated data. The DecontX workflow vignette that had that name is now vignette("decontX_RNA", package = "decontX"); its workflow is unchanged (#84).
  • decontX has a documentation website, https://campbio.github.io/decontX/, for the current Bioconductor release, and https://campbio.github.io/decontX/dev/ for the development version. Its address is in DESCRIPTION and the README (#84).

decontX 1.11.37

  • decontX() on a SingleCellExperiment with several batches now names the columns of each decontX_<batch>_UMAP DecontX_UMAP_1 and DecontX_UMAP_2, as in a single-batch run’s decontX_UMAP. They were UMAP_1 and UMAP_2, so code that reads these columns by name needs updating, and plotDecontXContamination() on one of them now titles its axes DecontX_UMAP_1 and DecontX_UMAP_2 (#99).
  • decontPro() now names its estimated parameters by ADT and droplet, from the row and column names of filtered_counts: the rows and columns of delta_est and background_est, the columns of r_est, and delta_mean_est and background_mean_est, which are now plain named vectors instead of 1-d arrays. Their values are unchanged (#129).
  • plotDensity() and plotBoxByCluster() now stop when counts and decontaminated_counts have different numbers of droplets, or column names that differ. They paired the two matrices by position, so they gave a wrong plot with no error (#125).
  • The README installs the development version from the devel branch. install_github("campbio/decontX") installs the current release (#137).

decontX 1.11.36

  • decontX() now matches the barcodes of background to the cells within each batch when batch and bgBatch are given. Before, a barcode that was a cell in one batch also removed the empty droplet with the same barcode in another, as happens with bare 10x barcodes from several samples. Results change slightly for such data (#134).
  • decontX() and decontPro() now warn when the called cells can’t be found in background by barcode: when the counts have no column names (only background without them warned before), and when no barcode matches but background has many droplets with as many counts as a typical cell (at least a tenth as many as there are cells, at or above the median cell’s total), as a raw matrix does when its barcodes are named differently from the cells’, for example without a sample prefix. These cells used to stay in the ambient profile without a word (#134).
  • decontPro() help and vignette say that background barcodes are matched across all droplets, so with several samples they must be unique across samples (#134).

decontX 1.11.35

  • decontPro() now removes the called cells from background, as decontX() does: droplets whose barcodes (column names) are also in filtered_counts are dropped, so the raw matrix can be given as it is. Before, their native signal went into the ambient profile, so results change for calls whose background included called cells. A background without column names gives a warning, and one with no droplets left, or no counts in the ADTs of filtered_counts, stops with a clear error instead of Stan’s “not a simplex” error (#131).

decontX 1.11.34

  • The decontPro vignette is rewritten. It uses the cord blood data’s own cell-type labels (no Seurat clustering), explains every output, shows how to tune the priors with before/after density plots, has a template for estimating the ambient profile from empty droplets with background, and covers run time, reproducibility, a FAQ and how to cite DecontPro. Stan’s progress no longer fills the page (#83).
  • decontPro() help describes every element it returns and says that only the ADT totals of background are used, so it must hold empty droplets only. Its example is smaller and seeded (#83).
  • dplyr is no longer suggested (#83).

decontX 1.11.33

  • decontPro() arguments are now camelCase, like decontX’s: cellType, deltaSd, backgroundSd, and background for the empty-droplet counts. The old names cell_type, delta_sd, background_sd and ambient_counts keep working as permanent aliases; giving both names of an argument is an error. Positional calls are unchanged. Two kinds of call that used to work now stop with an error: an abbreviated old name (such as ambient =, or background = for background_sd, since background now names the empty-droplet counts), and a positional value after an alias (such as cell_type = k, 1e-2) (#81).
  • New decontPro() arguments iter (default 50000) and seed (default
  1. control Stan’s fit; the defaults are the values used before, so results don’t change. verbose = FALSE hides decontPro’s messages and Stan’s console output, which is shown only if the fit fails (#81).
  • decontPro() deletes the temporary CSV that rstan writes, about 100 bytes per ADT x droplet, as soon as the fit ends; before, it stayed until R exited (#46, #81).
  • decontPro() help: deltaSd and backgroundSd are standard deviations of the priors, not variances, and background is described apart from the model’s background component (#81).

decontX 1.11.32

  • The decontX vignette shows the code that maps clusters to cell types, reuses the clusters for its second run, and splits “Running decontX” into runs without and with the background matrix, showing how to import the raw matrix and what decontX needs from it (#43). New sections cover multiple samples (#45) and a FAQ on data with one cell type (#43) and doublet detection (#44). It also says how to cite DecontX.
  • The package help page, the README and DESCRIPTION cite both papers.
  • Documentation fixes: contamination is a proportion between 0 and 1, not a percentage; simulateContamination() gives its real delta default (c(1, 10)) and lists everything it returns; decontXcounts() has an example (#83).

decontX 1.11.31

  • plotDensity() and plotBoxByCluster() now use a factor in features by its labels; before, they plotted the row at the factor’s integer code under the label’s title (#122). features must be rownames: row numbers, which used to select rows by position, now stop with an error. Empty features, features that aren’t rownames of both count matrices, and (in plotBoxByCluster()) a cell_type without one entry per droplet now stop with an error that names the argument. Before, a cell_type of the wrong length could be recycled silently, giving droplets the wrong cell types (#122, #123).

decontX 1.11.29

  • decontPro() splits the counts after the Stan fit with about half the memory and in less time. The split results can differ from before in the last digits (about 1e-16, relative); the estimated parameters are unchanged (#111).

decontX 1.11.28

  • decontPro() now stops with a clear error when the counts have a single ADT or a single droplet. Before, Stan failed with an unclear message about mismatched dimensions (#110).

decontX 1.11.26

  • decontX now needs scrapper 1.5.0 or later; every Bioconductor release since 3.23 ships one. Results are unchanged (#115).

decontX 1.11.25

  • Removed compiled code that nothing used, and the help pages of internal functions. The results of decontX(), decontPro() and simulateContamination() are unchanged (#78).

decontX 1.11.24

  • decontX no longer imports plyr or reshape2. Their few uses are now done in base R, with the same results (#77).

decontX 1.11.23

  • decontX() now stops with an error when batch or bgBatch contains an empty string (""). The estimates of a batch named "" couldn’t be read back by name, and its cells lost their cluster labels in z when decontX estimated the clusters or when the labels also appeared in another batch: every cell got "-" (or "" when it was the only batch). With more than one batch, a SingleCellExperiment and the default embedding = TRUE, the run failed with an unclear error while storing the UMAPs. Contamination and decontaminated counts were right (#102).

decontX 1.11.21

  • decontX() builds the decontaminated counts faster and with less memory: on 100,000 simulated cells with z given and embedding = FALSE, the run takes 1.2 s instead of 2.8 s and peaks about 1.2 GB lower. The native probability is now computed in the same direct form as in the EM, so the decontaminated counts can change in the last digits (at most about 1e-14 relative); contamination estimates are unchanged (#80).

decontX 1.11.20

  • decontX()’s EM step is faster: a run with cluster labels given in z and embedding = FALSE takes about half the time on the PBMC4k data (3.4 s to 1.7 s). The results are unchanged (#80).

decontX 1.11.19

  • New decontX() argument embedding. With embedding = FALSE and cluster labels given in z, decontX() skips the embedding (the normalization, variable genes, PCA and UMAP), which is most of the run time on large data sets. The decontamination is the same (except with legacyInit = TRUE and seed = NULL, where the EM’s random start differs); only the decontX UMAP is left out of the results. embedding = FALSE needs z, and lowers the minimum batch size from 3 cells (15 with legacyInit = TRUE) to 2 (#79).
  • New decontX() argument numThreads (default 1) for computing the embedding. With more than one thread the PCA can differ in the last digits on large data sets, which can move the UMAP coordinates and change estimated clusters: on 100,000 simulated cells, four threads found 11 clusters instead of 10. Set numThreads the same way to reproduce a run. With legacyInit = TRUE only the UMAP uses the threads (#79).
  • plotDecontXContamination() can plot the contamination on any reducedDim of a SingleCellExperiment with the new argument reducedDimName, for example after a run with embedding = FALSE. With reducedDimName and batch = NULL it plots every cell (#79).

decontX 1.11.17

  • With HDF5-backed counts, decontXcounts is now a DelayedMatrix held in memory instead of one written to a temporary HDF5 file. Runs are faster, and a saved object no longer points at a file that is deleted when the R session ends. The result needs memory for the sparse decontaminated counts, and HDF5Array’s dump settings (such as setHDF5DumpDir()) no longer apply to it. To keep it on disk, save it explicitly: HDF5Array::saveHDF5SummarizedExperiment() for a SingleCellExperiment, or HDF5Array::writeHDF5Array() for the matrix. Values don’t change (#76).

decontX 1.11.16

  • decontX() makes fewer copies of the decontaminated counts when it puts them together, so it allocates less memory and runs slightly faster, with or without batch. Results don’t change (#76).

decontX 1.11.15

  • decontX() stops when bgBatch is given with batch but without background. It used to ignore bgBatch then, unless its values didn’t match batch (#76).

decontX 1.11.14

  • decontX() on a matrix also returns batch, the batch of each cell used for the run ("all_cells" when batch isn’t given). The SingleCellExperiment results don’t change, apart from runParams below (#76).
  • runParams in the decontX() results always has batchBackground, which is NULL when background and bgBatch are both NULL. It used to be missing then (#96).

decontX 1.11.13

  • The marker plots’ error for duplicated groupClusters values has its missing space back (“assigned to a single group”) (#75).

decontX 1.11.12

  • simulateContamination() gives every cell NRange[1] counts when both ends of NRange are equal; it used to draw totals from 1 to that value. K = 1 now stops with a clear message: the simulated contamination comes from the other cell populations, so it needs at least two. So does a C too small to give two populations (for example C = 1). Both used to fail with “Division by 0” (#74).
  • retrieveFeatureIndex() never matches a feature that is NA, even when a row is named NA, and stops with a clear message when by isn’t a single string (#74).
  • runParams in the decontX() results also records seed and iterLogLik (#74).
  • Typos fixed in messages and help pages. The error for bgBatch given without batch now names both arguments, and the simulateContamination() help page names its outputs nativeCounts and observedCounts (#74).

decontX 1.11.11

  • plotDensity() smooths the original and decontaminated curves of an ADT with one bandwidth, computed from both. Each curve used to get its own, which made the less spread-out curve’s peaks look taller than they are (#73).
  • plotDensity() and plotBoxByCluster() save to file as given when it ends in “.pdf”; file = "x.pdf" used to write x.pdf.pdf. Without the extension, “.pdf” is still added. The help pages now say the path is returned invisibly (#73).
  • When groupClusters names labels that aren’t in z, the marker plots also list the labels z has. After a batched decontX() run, those can carry the batch as a prefix, such as "b1-1", which the help pages now explain (#73).
  • plotDecontXContamination() reads the UMAP columns by position, so a UMAP without column names, as after an h5ad round trip, plots instead of failing with .data[[NULL]] (#73).
  • The decontX() help page says a re-run keeps UMAPs from an earlier run with different batches in reducedDims (#73).
  • The decontPro vignette passes Seurat’s cluster identities to decontPro() as they are, so the cluster numbers in plotBoxByCluster() match the Seurat plots; they used to be shifted by one. Results don’t change (#73).

decontX 1.11.10

  • decontPro() reads every counts layer of a Seurat v5 object whose assay is split, joining them in Cells() order. It used to read only the first layer, with a warning, and either stop in Stan or run on that layer’s cells alone (#72).
  • decontPro() accepts any cell_type labels, such as integers with gaps, character strings or a factor, and recodes them for Stan. The rows of parameters$r_est are named by label. A cell_type of the wrong length or with NA, counts that aren’t non-negative whole numbers, and NA or negative values in ambient_counts stop with a clear message, and a failed Stan fit says so instead of stopping with “no applicable method for @”. Results for labels 1 to K don’t change (#72).
  • decontPro() stops on arguments it doesn’t know, such as seed, batch or a misspelled delta_SD, which used to be ignored (#72).

decontX 1.11.9

  • decontX() stops with a clear message when a batch, or x without batch, has fewer than 3 cells (15 with legacyInit = TRUE), which the initialization needs. A one-cell batch used to stop with “subscript out of bounds” (#71).
  • decontX() accepts a DelayedMatrix over a dense matrix, which used to stop after the whole run, and dgRMatrix and dgTMatrix counts without errors or deprecation warnings. Other inputs, such as a data.frame, a SummarizedExperiment or a matrix of logical or character values (logical sparse matrices used to run as 0/1 counts), stop with a message naming the class. With a SingleCellExperiment x, background must be a SingleCellExperiment too (#71).
  • decontXcounts is always a dgCMatrix, or a DelayedMatrix for DelayedArray input. dgTMatrix and SVT_SparseMatrix input used to come back in their own class. No results change (#71).

decontX 1.11.8

  • decontX() returns z as a factor. A supplied z comes back with its own labels instead of integer codes; a factor keeps its level order. In batched runs the labels get the batch prefix ("<batch>-<label>") only when a label is found in more than one batch. Estimated clusters keep their numbers ("<batch>-<k>" with batch). The phi and eta estimates are named by cluster label, and each batch’s estimates no longer holds z twice. as.integer(result$z) may give different values than before, and groupClusters in the marker plots now takes these labels for a supplied z (#70).
  • Unused levels in a factor z, including levels missing from one batch, no longer give NaN columns in phi. Contamination for such a z changes by about 1e-16; no other results change (#70).
  • plotDecontXMarkerPercentage() gives the right percentages and labels for any cluster labels; labels other than 1 to K used to stop, give NA labels or mislabel clusters. Both marker plots work with one marker gene or a groupClusters that keeps one cell, and plotDecontXMarkerExpression() no longer assigns cells to the wrong cluster when the cell names look like numbers (#70).

decontX 1.11.7

  • decontX() allows a z with one cluster when background is supplied, since the contamination profile then comes from the empty droplets. This fits only when the cells are a single cell type. Without background, one cluster still stops, and the error now names the batch (#69).
  • When dbscan finds only one cluster, the k-means fallback now runs on the PCA components instead of a dense matrix of all genes, which could need gigabytes of memory (#43). This changes the clusters and contamination estimates on that path only; legacyInit = TRUE still clusters all genes.
  • With legacyInit = TRUE, the k-means fallback no longer stops with “argument is not a matrix”. It had failed on this path since legacyInit was added, so no earlier results change.

decontX 1.11.6

  • decontX() now matches the rows of background to the genes of x by name, and decontPro() matches the rows of ambient_counts to the ADTs of filtered_counts. Before, rows were matched by position: rows in a different order ran without an error and gave wrong estimates, extra or missing genes gave a cryptic error (#43), and names that didn’t overlap ran. Now extra rows are dropped with a log message, missing genes stop with an error that names them, and rows are matched by position only when either matrix has no row names. Results don’t change when the rows already match (#68).
  • bgBatch must have one value per background droplet, with no NA, and its values must be the same as those of batch. Before, a short bgBatch was recycled, and a batch without matching background droplets silently ran without background. decontX() also stops when no background droplets are left after removing barcodes that are in x, and a batch with a single background droplet no longer fails.

decontX 1.11.5

  • decontX() now checks its inputs before running and stops with an error that names the argument. Before, a z or batch shorter than the number of cells was padded with NA and gave wrong results; z or batch with NA, invalid maxIter, iterLogLik, convergence, seed, varGenes, dbscanEps or logfile values, non-logical estimateDelta, legacyInit or verbose, a delta that isn’t two finite positive numbers, and negative counts in x or background ran silently or failed with cryptic errors. maxIter, iterLogLik and varGenes must be whole numbers (or Inf, which keeps working), and maxIter = Inf needs convergence above 0. An assayName or bgAssayName that isn’t an assay of the input now stops before decontX runs; an assay index still works. Results don’t change for valid input (#67).
  • The varGenes and legacyInit docs now say they still set the UMAP stored in the results when z is given, and the error for cells with no counts no longer suggests supplying z.

decontX 1.11.3

  • The “Working with Seurat” section of the decontX vignette now runs as pasted with SeuratObject 5: it reads counts with LayerData() instead of GetAssayData(slot = ) (defunct since SeuratObject 5.3), attaches SingleCellExperiment, and uses one name for the Seurat object (#65).

decontX 1.11.2

  • The decontX-package help page now has a Value section, which fixes a BiocCheck warning.
  • Documentation is regenerated with roxygen2 8.1.0, and the Stan model exports with rstantools 2.7.1. Results don’t change.

decontX 1.11.1

  • decontX no longer depends on the celda package (ADR-0003 Stage 1). The one internal use of celda::normalizeCounts() (proportion normalization inside simulateContamination()) is replaced by the package’s own fastNormProp routine, which produces identical results, and the example and vignette now plot cluster labels and marker-gene expression on the UMAP with scater::plotReducedDim() instead of celda’s plotting functions. This drops celda (and its transitive dependencies) entirely and removes the R CMD check deprecation warnings that came from celda’s masked, stale copy of decontX being invoked after library(celda) in the examples.
  • The cell cluster initialization used by decontX() when z is not supplied (log-normalization, variable gene selection, PCA, and UMAP) has been migrated from scater/scuttle to the scrapper package, because scuttle deprecated logNormCounts()/normalizeCounts() in Bioconductor 3.24. This removes the deprecation warnings from R CMD check.
  • Results of decontX() without z may differ slightly from previous versions (same workflow and parameters; different variable-gene criterion and UMAP implementation). A new legacyInit = TRUE argument reproduces the previous behavior; it requires the scater package (now in Suggests) and is kept for backwards compatibility for as long as the upstream functions remain available. Users supplying their own z are unaffected.
  • With the default initialization, the UMAP step itself is deterministic even when seed = NULL (scrapper seeds it explicitly), but overall decontX() results with seed = NULL remain non-reproducible because the EM initialization is unseeded — set a seed for full reproducibility.
  • The plotting functions (plotDecontXContamination(), plotDecontXMarkerPercentage(), plotDecontXMarkerExpression(), plotDensity(), plotBoxByCluster()) no longer use the deprecated ggplot2::aes_string() or trans = scale argument, which removes the ggplot2 deprecation warnings they emitted. decontX now requires ggplot2 (>= 3.5.0).
  • plotDecontXMarkerPercentage() and plotDecontXMarkerExpression() now work when x is a dense or sparse matrix (they previously failed with a ggplot2 aesthetics error when the plot was drawn). The facets of plotDecontXMarkerExpression() now follow the order of groupClusters, matching the x-axis.
  • decontPro() no longer draws 1000 unused samples from the variational posterior. Only the mean of the approximation is used, but the draws scaled with the number of ADTs x droplets and could take hundreds of GB of disk and memory on large datasets (#46). On a 50 x 400 test dataset the temporary file shrank from 444 MB to 2 MB and peak memory from 3.0 GB to 1.2 GB. Results are unchanged. rstan’s “Pareto k diagnostic” warning is no longer shown: it is estimated from the draws and would always report Inf with the minimal number of draws now requested.

decontX 1.10.0

  • No significant changes (Bioconductor 3.23 release).

decontX 1.8.0

  • No significant changes (Bioconductor 3.22 release).

decontX 1.6.0

  • No significant changes (Bioconductor 3.21 release). Includes the DecontPro changes released in 1.4.1 on the Bioconductor 3.20 branch.

decontX 1.4.1 (2025-02-16)

  • decontPro() gained an ambient_counts argument, so an empty-droplet count matrix can be supplied to estimate the ambient contamination profile empirically instead of inferring it from the filtered droplets.
  • Breaking: the first argument of decontPro() was renamed from object to filtered_counts for consistency with the new ambient_counts argument. Code that passed the count matrix by name (decontPro(object = x, ...)) must be updated; positional calls are unaffected.
  • The estimated ambient contamination profile is now returned in the parameters element of the decontPro() output (p_est).
  • Updated deprecated array syntax in the Stan model, fixed a C compiler warning in matrixSums, and corrected a deconPro typo in the DecontPro vignette.

decontX 1.4.0

  • No significant changes (Bioconductor 3.20 release).

decontX 1.2.0

  • No significant changes (Bioconductor 3.19 release).

decontX 1.0.0

  • First Bioconductor release (Bioconductor 3.18), providing decontX() for ambient RNA decontamination of single-cell RNA-seq counts and decontPro() for single-cell protein expression (CITE-seq/TotalSeq) data.

decontX 0.99.5 (2023-10-19)

  • First submission to Bioconductor after review.
